ChancePoints.Description: Fortune points the players can spend

ChancePointsRules.Gains: Fortune can be earned through remarkable actions, good ideas, good roleplaying and other praiseworthy behaviour...

0.Name: Impose banes
0.Description: A player can spend Fortune to impose 2 banes on any d20 roll. It is a great way to save someone's life by targeting a monster's attack roll or cancelling its boons. Or to give 2 banes to the Agility roll of an enemy pushed off a cliff so they miss their grip. One's Fortune is another's misfortune.

1.Name: Roll low
1.Description: A player can spend Fortune to change the result of any d6 to a 1. This neutralizes an opponent's boon by reducing its bonus to 1, forces someone to fail a fate roll in the worst possible way, or reduces incoming damage to avoid falling unconscious. Bringing bad luck on others may not be honourable, but neither are these times.

2.Name: Remove an affliction
2.Description: When a member of the group is about to gain an affliction (other than defenseless or unconscious), any player can spend Fortune to immediately cancel that affliction on that character, avoiding disastrous consequences.

3.Name: Refuse a Mark of Darkness
3.Description: A player whose character would gain a Mark of Darkness can spend Fortune to refuse it. Not every practitioner of the dark arts wants to display their depravity. It lets them hide their Corruption from the Inquisition... or from their own companions.

4.Name: Control Madness
4.Description: A player about to go mad can spend Fortune to take the Revelation result instead of the result rolled on the d20 Madness table. Revelation strengthens the character's resolve against monstrosities, at least for a while.

5.Name: Stay Death's hand
5.Description: A player whose character takes damage equal to or greater than their Health can spend Fortune to become merely incapacitated instead of dying instantly. If there is one reason to keep Fortune, this is it. Instant death rules remind players they are not invincible; this option saves them from a crushing attack or a tragic fall, even if it does not protect them from what comes next.

6.Name: Improvised magic
6.Description: A player who has discovered at least one magic tradition can spend Fortune to sacrifice a casting of a learned spell and instead cast any other spell of equal or lower rank from a tradition they have discovered. It lets them cast exactly the right spell at the right time.

7.Name: Alter reality
7.Description: A player can spend Fortune to slightly alter the story to keep the narrative moving. This is the most open use and requires strict GM control. Usually it gets around a complication: finding the key to a locked door, discovering a 20-metre rope when 10 were missing, or finding a witness in a crowded street. As it can completely defuse a plot, the GM is free to refuse or adjust the result to fit the story.

FortuneAwardsTable.Title: Fortune Award Frequency
FortuneAwardsTable.Subtitle: Maximum awards by group size
FortuneAwardsTable.Note: A small group has three characters or fewer, a large group has six or more.

Deafened.Name: Deafened
Deafened.Description: Cannot hear anything (Perception rolls based on hearing fail).

Prone.Name: Prone
Prone.Description: 1 bane on Strength/Agility rolls. Enemies get 1 boon to attack in melee and 1 bane at range. Standing up costs the move or an action.

Blinded.Name: Blinded
Blinded.Description: Speed 2 at most, cannot see anything.

Charmed.Name: Charmed
Charmed.Description: Considers the source a trusted ally and cannot target it.

Compelled.Name: Compelled
Compelled.Description: Cannot act or move; on each fast turn, the source can force it to move or use an action.

Frightened.Name: Frightened
Frightened.Description: 1 bane on rolls (3 if it can see the source), cannot take fast turns.

Asleep.Name: Asleep
Asleep.Description: Prone and unconscious. A creature can use an action to wake the character. Taking damage wakes it.

Grabbed.Name: Grabbed
Grabbed.Description: If its Size is equal to or smaller than the attacker's, cannot move away from it; otherwise the attacker can follow its movement or let go.

Immobilized.Name: Immobilized
Immobilized.Description: Speed 0 and 1 boon to attack the character.

Stunned.Name: Stunned
Stunned.Description: Cannot act or move, 1 boon to attack it.

Surprised.Name: Surprised
Surprised.Description: Cannot act or move (for this round).

Horrified.Name: Horrified
Horrified.Description: 3 banes on rolls while it can see the source of its horror.

Defenseless.Name: Defenseless
Defenseless.Description: Cannot act, Defense 5, every roll fails (except Perception).

0.Name: Attack / Cast a spell / Reload a weapon
0.Description: Perform an action not listed here, as the player imagines it.

1.Name: Help
1.Description: Intellect roll to give 1 boon to a creature.

2.Name: Prepare
2.Description: Declare an action and a trigger. If the action triggers, the rolls for that action get 1 boon.

4.Name: Search
4.Description: Find and share the location of a hidden creature.

5.Name: Concentrate
5.Description: On a spell. It is lost if the character takes damage and fails a Will roll, or does something else.

6.Name: Dismiss
6.Description: End the effect of a still-active spell cast by the character.

7.Name: Hide
7.Description: Behind cover, in the shadows... A creature that cannot see the character has 3 banes against it, and the character 1 boon against it.

8.Name: Defend
8.Description: Enemy attacks take 1 bane and the character gets 1 boon on defensive rolls.

10.Name: Stabilize
10.Description: Intellect roll (1 bane if the creature is dying) to heal 1 damage on an incapacitated creature.

11.Name: Use an item / Reload
11.Description: Use an item or reload a weapon.

0.Name: Disengaging attack
0.Description: 1 bane. On a success, the target gets no free attack against the character this round.

1.Name: Defensive attack
1.Description: 1 bane; the next attack targeting the character takes 1 bane.

2.Name: Staggering attack
2.Description: 1 bane; a target of equal or smaller Size falls prone if it fails its Agility roll.

4.Name: Driving attack
4.Description: 1 bane, move [Strength mod] metres, dragging the target along.

0.Name: Called shot
0.Description: 2 banes to aim at a specific part (for example the eyes, to impose 1 bane).

1.Name: Long shot
1.Description: 1 bane to shoot beyond normal range.

2.Name: Knockdown shot
2.Description: 2 banes against a target of equal or smaller Size; it falls prone if it fails its Agility roll.

0.Name: Two weapons
0.Description: 2 banes, deals the damage of both weapons. Or 3 banes for 2 attacks against 2 different targets.

1.Name: Disarm
1.Description: Agility/Strength roll against Agility/Strength (2 banes if unarmed).

2.Name: Distract
2.Description: Intellect attack roll to impose 2 banes on the target's next roll.

3.Name: Grab
3.Description: Agility/Strength roll against Agility. Costs an action each round to maintain.

4.Name: Escape
4.Description: If grabbed: Agility/Strength roll against Strength.

5.Name: Feint
5.Description: Agility against Perception. Grants 2 boons on the character's next roll against the target's Defense or Agility, or avoids free attacks.

6.Name: Knock down (standing)
6.Description: Strength against Agility (1 bane per larger Size, 1 boon if smaller) to knock the target prone.

7.Name: Knock down (grabbed)
7.Description: Strength against Strength for a grabbed target no larger. On a success, move at half Speed.

8.Name: Shove
8.Description: Strength against Strength (1 bane per larger Size, 1 boon if smaller). Pushes 1 + [Strength mod] metres.

9.Name: Charge
9.Description: Move, taking 1 bane on all rolls this round. Allows an attack, shove or knock down.

0.Name: Cover
0.Description: Can impose 1 or 2 banes on enemy attacks, or make them fail against total cover.

1.Name: Darkness
1.Description: A dim / dark / totally dark area imposes 1 / 2 / 3 banes on attacks.

OutOfCombat.Content: An incapacitated character is defenseless and makes a fate roll (1d6) each round. They can start dying (1), get back up impaired (6), or stay unconscious for a few hours (after 3 rounds). A dying character keeps rolling and can die (1), or become incapacitated again (6). Injured: from half Health.

Madness.Content: Gaining Insanity: when the character gains Insanity, they become frightened for rounds equal to their total Insanity. If already frightened, Will roll or be stunned for one round. Going mad: if total Insanity reaches Will, the character suffers a Madness then loses 1d6 + [Will mod] Insanity.

Corruption.Content: Gaining Corruption: by committing atrocious acts. Then roll 1d20 and gain a Mark of Darkness if the roll does not exceed total Corruption. Effects: from 4 Corruption, the character suffers additional effects.

Spellcasting.Formula: It must be spoken, so the caster must be able to speak.
Spellcasting.Focus: It must be brandished. It is an item such as a wand, an amulet, a grimoire...
Spellcasting.UseCost: Spend a casting, regained after a rest.
Spellcasting.NonConsenting: Unwilling target: make an attack roll (Intellect or Will) against the target's Agility.

Incantation.Description: These are formulas written on a scroll, carved, painted...
Incantation.Cast: To use it: Intellect roll. The incantation is then destroyed.
Incantation.PowerVsLevel: If the spell's rank exceeds the character's Power, the roll takes banes equal to the difference.
Incantation.HigherPower: If the character's Power is higher, no roll is needed.
